text: Lessons 17 and 18 built real, working checks. But a script that runs on a schedule and prints its result to a console nobody is watching has the same gap as the original problem — someone still has to remember to go look. Alerting is the last piece.

Send-OverlookAlert keeps the mechanism deliberately simple: Send-MailMessage, emailing the on-call DBA automatically when a condition fails. A larger environment might use Azure Monitor action groups or a paging service, but the underlying idea is identical.

Wiring in Lesson 17's health check and Lesson 18's backup test is a few real lines: if OverallHealthy comes back false, or BackupVerified comes back false, send an alert. Run on a schedule, this means the on-call DBA finds out within one scheduling interval, automatically.

Lesson 1 described access and process depending on whoever happened to be on call. This is the direct technical answer: the checks run regardless of who's thinking about them, and the alert reaches whoever is actually on call. Next chapter builds the ongoing data feed that keeps this automated platform fed.
